subject: Production API: edge proxy failover causing high latency & 5xx surge
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@quantumretail.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops+qa@quantumretail.com
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Latency and 5xx spike in production (urgent)

Hey Kimberly,

We're seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end latency for Redwood API calls from our checkout region (us-west-2). Error rates spiked to ~12% for text generation around 09:00 PDT and throughput dropped by ~30%. Attaching a sample of request IDs and timestamps.

Symptoms we observe: 
- Intermittent 504/502 responses from the API
- Long TCP connect times (~600-900ms) before TLS handshake sometimes
- Errors correlate with a backend proxy failover on our side (we saw a flurry of SYN retransmits)

This is affecting live transactions. Can Redwood confirm whether there were any routing changes or peering events affecting us? We need a short RCA and mitigations.

Thanks,
Liam
Sr. SRE, Quantum Retail

Attachments: request-sample-quantum-08-20.txt

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-20T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Latency and 5xx spike in production (urgent)

Marcus / Diego — forwarding an urgent report from Quantum Retail (prod, us-west-2). They observe 5xx surge and elevated connect times that line up with a customer-side proxy failover, but the timings also coincide with a VPC peering route flap we saw in telemetry at 09:02 PDT.

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: run a quick correlation between our ingress logs and the customer's request IDs (I included sample IDs). Look at connection durations, backend selection, and any DNS timeouts from our edge.
- Diego: check VPC peering health, NAT device session counts, and any firewall policy churn between us-west-2 and their VPC.

Please reply with findings and a recommended mitigation we can give the customer within 30 minutes. I'm standing by to loop in Ops/CS/Execs.

-Kim
Senior AM, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-20T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency and 5xx spike in production (urgent)

On Thu, Aug 20, 2026 at 09:25, kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
> Marcus / Diego — forwarding an urgent report from Quantum Retail (prod, us-west-2).

Quick summary from the serving side: correlated customer request IDs match higher P95 connect times starting at 09:00 PDT. We saw a short window (~09:01:30–09:05:00) where our edge observed repeated DNS A lookups for the customer's proxy host and ~200ms additional DNS latency for a subset of client IPs.

Preliminary hypothesis: two concurrent issues:
- Customer-side proxy failover produced SYN bursts and transient retransmits.
- Our edge experienced a transient increase in DNS resolution latency (resolver cluster rebalanced) which amplified connection setup time, pushing some requests past upstream timeouts and causing 502/504s.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (we can push to the customer):
1) On Redwood edge: temporarily increase upstream connect timeout to 5s for Quantum Retail routes and enable circuit-breaker fallback to alternate origin.
2) Ask the customer to short-circuit the proxy failover (stick to healthy backends) and reduce client-side retry storms (backoff).
3) If no quick fix, route Quantum traffic to a warm standby region (us-east-1) for the next 60 minutes.

I'll attach the edge log slice and the DNS timing summary.

Attachments: edge-log-quantum-09-01-30.txt, dns-summary-09-01-30.csv

-marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency and 5xx spike in production (urgent)

Attaching packet captures and NAT/session counters from the us-west-2 egress cluster. Findings:
- NAT ephemeral port exhaustion observed on a subset of egress nodes (session table near 98% capacity) leading to TCP resets and retries.
- Several firewall devices showed flapping for the peering route to the customer's VPC between 09:00:50–09:03:20.
- DNS resolver node 3 had a GC pause and delayed response to recursive queries at 09:01:12 (adds ~150–250ms to resolution for some clients).

Root cause (working hypothesis): simultaneous customer proxy failover plus our peering path instability + NAT exhaustion = amplified connect latency and 502/504s.

Immediate actions taken by infra:
- Cleared session tables on affected NAT nodes and bumped ephemeral port pools where possible.
- Kicked DNS resolver node 3 to promote replacement and rebalanced the resolver cluster.
- We are temporarily steering Quantum Retail routes to alternate egress nodes with spare capacity.

I'll follow up with a timeline and the pcap excerpts.

Attachments: network-trace-20260820.pcap, nat-counters-08-20.txt

-Diego
Network Reliability Engineer

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Bcc: vp-eng@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-21T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary & next steps — Quantum Retail production incident (08/20)

Anika / Liam —

Thanks again for flagging this. Below is a concise summary for your leadership and ours, plus the immediate mitigation actions and next steps. Please let me know if you'd like this reformatted into a one-page PDF (attached) for your CTO.

Summary (what happened)
- 09:00–09:05 PDT (08/20): Customer-side proxy failover triggered a burst of new TCP connections from Quantum Retail. Concurrently, Redwood observed a brief peering route instability and elevated load on a subset of egress NAT devices. A DNS resolver node also experienced a GC pause that added ~150–250ms for some recursive lookups. The combination pushed several connection attempts past upstream timeouts and generated increased 502/504 responses and higher latency.

Customer impact
- P95 latency increase (~400–900ms additional connect time) and ~12% 5xx rate for a 4-minute window; throughput drop ~30% for checkout traffic in us-west-2.

Immediate mitigations executed
- Cleared NAT session tables and increased ephemeral port capacity on affected egress nodes.
- Rebalanced DNS resolvers and replaced a paused node.
- Temporarily increased upstream connect timeout to 5s and enabled circuit-breaker fallback for Quantum routes.
- Steered traffic to alternate egress nodes to reduce pressure while customer stabilizes proxy.

Short-term recommendations (action items)
- Customer: Temporarily disable aggressive proxy failover and apply exponential backoff for retries during handovers.
- Redwood: Deploy a per-account temporary routing policy for Quantum Retail to direct traffic to warm-standby region if similar symptoms reappear.

Next steps & accountability
- Diego: full network timeline and packet capture analysis (ETA 3 hours).
- Marcus: post-incident log correlation and a short change to default connect timeouts for affected tenants (ETA 6 hours).
- Kimberly (me): prepare customer-facing one-page incident summary and schedule a 30-minute retrospective with your network/SRE team tomorrow.

We're treating this as high priority — I've BCC'd our VP Eng for visibility. Apologies for the disruption; we'll follow up with the full timeline and the attachments we referenced.

Attachments: exec-summary-quantum-08-21.pdf

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
